evidence: start: [What happened; How did we respond] Customer-facing latency and packet loss began at 10:33 UTC on 14 March 2024, about half an hour after the west coast cable cuts. end: [What happened; How did we respond] Capacity shifted from the Lagos edge at 11:00 UTC on 15 March ended the last WAN packet drops and mitigated customer impact. regions: [Title; What happened] Customers in both South African regions, South Africa North and South Africa West, saw connectivity failures.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 03/14/2024 matches the incident start date and the text cites later completions, so it is not taken as the publication date. Two named regions, so multi_region; no zone named. End is the stated end of customer impact; the incident was only declared mitigated at 2024-03-18T02:00Z after emergency capacity came online, which is not used. services_n counts the 21 downstream services listed by name; the broad categories also named (Compute, Storage, Networking, Databases, App Services, Microsoft 365) are not counted as distinct products.

evidence: start: [What happened; timeline] Customers first felt ARM failures at 01:30 UTC on 21 January 2024 as capacity loss spread across large ARM regions. end: [How did we respond; timeline] West Europe, the last region, recovered at 08:58 UTC, ending most customer impact and fully mitigating the ARM incident. regions: [What happened] Impact concentrated in Central US, East US, South Central US, West Central US and West Europe, with lesser effects possible elsewhere.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 01/21/2024 matches the incident date and the text cites later work, so it is not taken as the publication date. Scope coded multi_region on the five named regions; the report adds that other regions may have seen lesser impact because ARM is global, but does not say all regions were affected. region_starts left empty: the timeline gives only detection times of additional impact (East US and West Europe 03:04 UTC, South Central US 03:30 UTC), not stated starts. Other regions recovered at 05:30 UTC; Key Vault in West Europe recovered at 09:28 UTC, after the coded end. services_n is ARM plus 25 named downstream services; Azure CLI, PowerShell and the portal are access channels and are not counted.

evidence: start: [What happened; What went wrong] A 1.9-second power loss at 07:24 UTC on 16 September 2023 rebooted scale units, starting VM connectivity problems. end: [What happened; timeline] By 19:00 UTC all compute and SQL nodes were recovered, closing the stated impact window. regions: [What happened] The power event hit one datacenter in a single Availability Zone of East US; zonal Service Bus and Event Hubs kept working.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 09/16/2023 matches the incident date and the text cites later communications (19 September), so it is not taken as the publication date. Scope zonal: one Availability Zone affected, but the report does not name or number it, so zones is empty. 19:00 UTC is both the stated end of the impact window and the declared full mitigation. services_n counts Virtual Machines, SQL Database, Service Bus and Event Hubs.

evidence: start: [What happened; timeline] Customer impact began around 10:30 UTC on 30 August 2023 when overheating equipment started shutting itself down. end: [What happened; timeline] Most services were back by 22:40 UTC that day, when 99% of VMs had recovered. regions: [What happened; AKS section] One of three Australia East zones lost cooling; AKS operations in Australia Southeast also failed through a shared database.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 08/30/2023 matches the incident date and the text refers to later revisions of the preliminary PIR, so it is not taken as the publication date. Impact centred on one unnamed Availability Zone of Australia East (zones empty), but the report names AKS CRUD impact in Australia Southeast, so coded multi_region; ARM errors also reached customers worldwide for resource groups homed in Australia East. The 08:41 UTC voltage sag preceded customer impact and is not the start. End is the time most services recovered; full mitigation came at 2023-09-03T20:00Z (last SQL ring), and some storage accounts recovered on 1 September, which are not used. services_n counts the 49 named Azure services; Microsoft 365 and Power Platform, named only as service families, are not counted.

evidence: start: [What happened; timeline] External customers were first affected at 23:15 UTC on 6 July 2023 once cached configuration expired. end: [What happened; timeline] At 09:00 UTC on 7 July control plane errors and latency returned to normal and the incident was declared mitigated. regions: [What happened] The report states that customers in every region were affected.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 07/06/2023 matches the incident start date, so it is not taken as the publication date. Scope global because the report says customers in all regions were impacted; no region codes apply. Control plane problems were detected at 12:30 UTC on 6 July, but the report states customer impact began only at 23:15 UTC. 09:00 UTC closes the stated impact window and is also the mitigation declaration. services_n counts Azure Monitor Log Analytics, Microsoft Sentinel and Diagnostic Settings log routing; the routing destinations (Storage, Event Hub, Marketplace) and Azure Container Apps (source of the faulty deployment) are not counted as impaired services.

evidence: start: [What happened; How did we respond] Packet loss and latency began at roughly 07:22 UTC on 5 July 2023, when alerts flagged the fiber cut. end: [What happened; How did we respond] By 16:00 UTC packet drops were back to normal levels after traffic rebalancing and throttling. regions: [What happened] West Europe intra-region traffic was congested; Azure Databricks also saw impact in North Europe through a control plane dependency.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 07/05/2023 matches the incident date, so it is not taken as the publication date. Primary impact was West Europe; North Europe is named only for Azure Databricks, which makes two named regions, so coded multi_region. Start is given as approximate. Fiber repair finished 20:50 UTC and mitigation was declared at 22:45 UTC; neither is used because impact ended at 16:00 UTC. services_n counts 17 named Azure services plus Microsoft Sentinel; Microsoft 365 and Power Platform, named only as families with affected subsets, are not counted.

evidence: start: [What happened] Portal access errors began at 15:10 UTC on 9 June 2023. end: [What happened; How did we respond] Monitoring showed every Azure Portal endpoint healthy again at 17:00 UTC. regions: [What went wrong; How did we respond] The DDoS-driven unavailability appeared across several geographies and the report refers to limiting global impact; no Azure region is named.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 06/09/2023 matches the incident date, so it is not taken as the publication date. Scope coded global because the report speaks of global impact and of the portal failing in multiple geographies; it names no region, so regions is empty. services_n counts the Azure Portal, the Microsoft Entra admin center and Microsoft Intune.

evidence: start: [What happened; How did we respond] ARM management problems started at 02:20 UTC on 23 March 2023, the first measurable drop from normal performance. end: [What happened; How did we respond] By 07:30 UTC regional ARM availability was back above 99.999%. regions: [What happened] Failures were confined to ARM requests processed in West Europe, up to half of that region's calls.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 03/23/2023 matches the incident date, so it is not taken as the publication date. Mitigation was confirmed at 07:54 UTC, after the coded impact end. services_n counts Azure Resource Manager only; Azure CLI, PowerShell and the portal are clients of ARM, and dependent Azure services are mentioned without names.

evidence: start: [What happened] Excess Storage throttling for some customers started at 03:50 UTC on 6 March 2023. end: [What happened] The stated impact window for throttling and dependent service failures closes at 17:55 UTC. regions: [What happened] Affected Storage resources were those located in West Europe, on a small set of scale units.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 03/06/2023 matches the incident date, so it is not taken as the publication date. End uses the impact window in What happened (17:55 UTC); the response section says impacted resources were mitigated by 16:34 UTC, earlier than the stated window end, which is noted but not used. services_n counts Azure Storage plus 12 named dependent services, with ExpressRoute and ExpressRoute Gateways counted once.

evidence: start: [What happened; Chiller failures section] At 20:19 UTC on 7 February 2023 thermal warnings forced infrastructure shutdown in one Southeast Asia zone, beginning customer impact. end: [Chiller failures section] Most customers had platform services back by 16:30 UTC on 8 February; a few services lagged. regions: [What happened; Impact to the ARM service] Southeast Asia lost one zone; ARM traffic shifted to East Asia overloaded it, so both regions saw impact.
notes: no publication date shown; the unlabeled header date 02/07/2023 matches the incident start date and the text cites later completed actions, so it is not taken as the publication date. The affected Southeast Asia Availability Zone is not named, so zones is empty. The 15:17 UTC voltage dip preceded customer impact and is not the start. region_starts left empty: East Asia impact followed the ARM traffic shift completed at 04:10 UTC on 8 February, but the report gives no explicit East Asia start time. End is the time most customers recovered; the final SQL tenant ring recovered at 2023-02-09T04:30Z, which is not used. services_n counts the 29 named degraded services plus the Azure portal and ARM; the BCDR services (Site Recovery, Backup, GRS Storage) are already in that list.
